title: Method C State Transfer Audit, Force Discontinuity, and Coarse Pinning Forensic Report

analytical_coarsening_formula.formula: xi * coth(xi) - 1, where xi = h / (2 * l0)
analytical_coarsening_formula.reconciliation_note: The 1D analytical formula xi*coth(xi)-1 yields +53.25% locally on h=20 um elements. In the 2D finite element model, the total integrated damage error is +5.0465% because damage is localized (over 97% of the domain d ~ 0) and 2D bilinear quad Gauss quadrature differs from 1D linear chords. Criterion 3 strictly fails the 5.0% threshold.

criterion_3_integrated_damage.qualification: Exceeds strict 5.0% threshold by +0.0465% (evaluated 5.0465%). Classified as FAIL under strict threshold governance. The discrepancy is a 2D domain-integrated numerical quadrature difference over nonmatching elements. While the 1D infinite-domain analytical formula xi*coth(xi)-1 yields +53.25% locally on h=20 um elements, the 2D domain-integrated error is damped to +5.05% because >97% of the specimen has d ~ 0 and 2D bilinear quad quadrature differs from 1D linear chords. The 1D formula does not prove 2D domain compliance, so Criterion 3 remains strictly FAIL.

criterion_5_boundary_force_continuity.qualification: Evaluated across the actual Abaqus step boundary: |RF_step2_inc1 - RF_step1_end| = |653.1694 - 674.7167| = 21.55 N (exceeds 5.0 N threshold by +16.55 N). Classified as FAIL under strict threshold governance. Step 1 functions mechanically as a one-increment reload from zero displacement; coarse-mesh secant stiffness over Delta u = 0.0050 mm yields RF = 674.72 N, whereas the true tangent at Step 2 entry drops to 653.17 N. Comparing donor (653.09 N) to Step 2 entry (653.17 N) yields Delta RF = 0.0794 N, but cherry-picking this subset comparison obscures the physical 21.55 N handoff discontinuity in the executed solver trajectory.

donor_mesh.name: M1_MB_NATIVE_FINAL_1S.inp
donor_mesh.provenance: Generated by native Abaqus adaptiveRemesh on Step-1 MISESERI with errorTarget=1.0

mesh_adaptivity_lineage.distinction_note: Package 41 evaluates the feasibility of nonmatching state transfer and static continuation architecture without reload from zero. Because it maps from 14.7k down to 2.9k, it is NOT an adaptive refinement cycle. Validated sequential adaptive refinement requires the forward coarse-to-fine progression (e.g. 2,906 FE -> 14,677 FE).

step_1_re_equilibration.analysis: Step 1 converges in 1 increment (2 iters) resolving compatible displacement and phase fields with 99.93% internal energy preservation (0.07% error). The end-of-step reaction force is 674.72 N (+21.63 N vs donor) due to coarse-mesh stiffness over the single large handoff increment.

step_2_continuation_entry.analysis: Across the actual step boundary, RF drops from 674.72 N to 653.17 N (Delta RF = 21.55 N), strictly FAILING the 5.0 N threshold. The entry tangent agrees with the donor (653.09 N vs 653.17 N, Delta RF = 0.0794 N), but this tangent relaxation occurs across the boundary discontinuity.

coarse_mesh_crack_pinning_audit.pinning_mechanism: Because h/l0 = 2.67 > 1, the element size exceeds the regularization length scale l0 = 7.5 um. The regularized damage band (width ~ 2*l0 = 15 um) cannot localize within a single element column. Consequently, the discrete damage profile is artificially broadened, causing severe crack pinning, elevated initiation resistance, delayed post-peak softening, and peak reaction force climbing past 880 N towards F_max ~ 1.08 kN (matching Gate C1 V2 Job 1412464 at 1.0868 kN vs reference 0.7578 kN).
coarse_mesh_crack_pinning_audit.scientific_conclusion: Successful convergence of Step 1 re-equilibration verifies state-transfer data structures and initial static equilibrium, but does NOT demonstrate sequential adaptive fracture propagation. The 14.7k -> 2.9k coarsening run is an offline data-structure qualification, not an accurate fracture mechanics simulation.

forward_refinement_design.scientific_objective: Evaluate true adaptive refinement (coarse donor 2.9k -> fine recipient 14.7k) to eliminate coarse-mesh crack pinning and achieve reference-level peak load (~0.743-0.758 kN).
